---
name: chrome-devtools
description: >
  Drive a real Chromium browser through the mcp__chrome_devtools__* tools: open
  pages, read and interact with them via uid snapshots, take screenshots, check
  console errors and network requests. Use whenever a task involves viewing,
  testing, debugging, or interacting with a web page or web app — verifying
  frontend changes, reproducing UI bugs, checking rendered output, or reading a
  page that needs JavaScript. NEVER install or use puppeteer, playwright, or
  selenium; a browser is already available through these tools.
---

# Chrome DevTools browser

A Chromium instance (isolated profile) is available through the
`mcp__chrome_devtools__*` tools, backed by the chrome-devtools-mcp server via
pi's built-in MCP support. The first call launches the browser — expect a few
seconds of cold start.

## Direct tools

| Tool | Use for |
|---|---|
| `mcp__chrome_devtools__new_page` | Open a URL in a new tab (also starts the browser) |
| `mcp__chrome_devtools__navigate_page` | Navigate the selected page, go back/forward |
| `mcp__chrome_devtools__wait_for` | Wait for text to appear — use instead of sleeping |
| `mcp__chrome_devtools__take_snapshot` | Accessibility-tree text snapshot; every element gets a `uid` |
| `mcp__chrome_devtools__take_screenshot` | PNG/JPEG of viewport, full page, or one element |
| `mcp__chrome_devtools__click` | Click an element by `uid` |
| `mcp__chrome_devtools__fill` | Type into an input or select by `uid` |
| `mcp__chrome_devtools__evaluate_script` | Run a JS function in the page, get JSON back |
| `mcp__chrome_devtools__list_console_messages` | Console output since load |
| `mcp__chrome_devtools__list_network_requests` | Requests with status, type, size |

## Core workflow

1. `mcp__chrome_devtools__new_page` with the URL.
2. `mcp__chrome_devtools__take_snapshot` → read the uid-labeled tree.
3. Interact by uid: `mcp__chrome_devtools__click`, `mcp__chrome_devtools__fill`.
4. Re-snapshot after anything that changes the DOM — uids go stale.

Snapshot vs screenshot: snapshots are cheap, text-based, and enough for
"what's on the page / click X / is Y shown". Screenshot only for genuinely
visual questions (layout, styling, images, canvas).

`mcp__chrome_devtools__evaluate_script` covers state neither shows — computed
styles, localStorage, app state. Pass a function: `() => document.title`,
or with an element: `(el) => el.value` plus the uid argument.

## Debugging recipes

- Page misbehaving? Reproduce it first, then
  `mcp__chrome_devtools__list_console_messages` for errors and
  `mcp__chrome_devtools__list_network_requests` for failed or slow requests.
- More tools are deferred (not declared until loaded): `hover`, `drag`,
  `fill_form`, `press_key`, `handle_dialog`, `resize_page`, `emulate`,
  performance tracing, `lighthouse_audit`, memory snapshots, and
  `get_network_request` / `get_console_message` for single-item detail.
  Load them with `tool_search` (e.g. query "chrome performance trace"), then
  call them directly, e.g. `mcp__chrome_devtools__performance_start_trace`.

## Rules

- Never install puppeteer, playwright, selenium, or chromedriver — this
  browser is already here.
- Never sleep or poll to wait for a page; use `mcp__chrome_devtools__wait_for`.
- If `mcp__chrome_devtools__*` tools are missing from your tool list, the
  server is not connected: ask the user to check `/mcp` (or run
  `/mcp reconnect chrome-devtools`).
- Configuration (Chromium path, which tools are direct) lives in
  `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json`.
